subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make agent filesystem tools workspace-contained by default for existing host-mode users, and how should exec/process access and upgrade compatibility be handled?
rationale: The source-level issue is real, but the fix changes a security/default compatibility boundary rather than a small isolated defect.

options.title: Define secure default with migration
options.body: Make workspace containment the default for file tools, document any opt-out, and add doctor/docs/tests for upgrade behavior plus a separate exec boundary decision.

options.title: Keep opt-in only
options.body: Leave current host-wide behavior documented and improve warnings, setup guidance, and sandbox recommendations without changing defaults.

options.title: Defer to broader isolation
options.body: Keep this open until broader per-agent isolation or filesystem roots work lands, accepting that current file tools remain opt-in protected.

recommendation.title: Define secure default with migration
recommendation.body: Make workspace containment the default for file tools, document any opt-out, and add doctor/docs/tests for upgrade behavior plus a separate exec boundary decision.
